row: Establish a head of the parking operation

1. Eliminate the designation of on-street parking spaces for use only by the residents of
one particular property
2. Forbid charter bus and other large vehicle parking within designated neighborhoods
3. Remove the 2-hour meters from the 300 block of W. 9th Street
5. Change a number of 2-hour meters to 10-hour meters
7. Increase the cost of right-of-way (meter bagging) permits

8. Investigate the potential of adding parallel parking on the west side of Rhode Island
Street
9. Establish a boot and tow policy to deal with habitual parking violators
10. Establish a residential permit parking policy for the city’s neighborhoods
11. Review zoning ordinance requirements regarding downtown residential parking
12. Establish a reserve fund for parking
13. Work with Douglas County to solve the parking issues at the Law Enforcement Center

14. Improve wayfinding signage from Massachusetts Street and major approaches to
Downtown to surface parking lots and garages

15. Add multi-space, pay-by-plate kiosks on-street, which would permit license plate
enforcement, use of credit cards and cell phone payments
16. Add multi-space, pay-by-plate kiosks in the off-street parking facilities

17. Acquire license plate recognition software and vehicles to enforce on- and off-street
parking

18. Acquire software or develop a web portal allowing for online payment of parking
violations and purchasing of monthly/annual parking permits
19. Increase the rate charged on Massachusetts Street from $0.50/hr. to $1.00/hr.
20. Increase the rate charged at 10-hour meters and 10-hour garage spaces to $0.20/hr.

22. Increase initial fines for metered/timed parking violations to $10.00 and on repeat
offenders to $100, with booting/towing automatically after 3 unpaid tickets
23. Establish a monthly (overnight) permit for downtown residents in one of the garages
24. Change existing parking ordinance relative to meter feeding
25. Restripe parking lots to increase the number of spaces

26. Review lighting in all parking facilities and replace where appropriate with energy-
efficient fixtures
27. Extend meter hours in active areas to 9PM on weekdays and Saturdays
